newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU investigates German, Spanish subsidies.
newsitem.headline: EU investigates German, Spanish subsidies.

text.p: The European Commission said on Friday it had opened investigations into government aid granted to German porcelain company Triptis Porzellan GmbH and Spanish ceramics company Ponsal.

It said in a statement it would examine the decision by state-owned bank Hessische Landesbank to waive 10 million marks ($5.8 million) of a debt package to help Triptis, located in the former East Germany, to restructure following its privatisation.
The Commission said it doubted whether the bank was acting as a private banker would and noted that Triptis was operating in a market suffering from strong overcapacity.
The European Union executive said it was also investigating subsidies provided by Navarra province for a 3-billion-peseta ($20.7 million) sanitation plan drafted in 1994 by Ponsal.
It said the aid included a guarantee of 1.2 billion pesetas, a job-creation subsidy of 100 million pesetas and a 20 percent subsidy for investment in fixed assets.

Spanish authorities have informed the Commission that Ponsal has filed for bankruptcy and its activities taken over by a new company called Commercial Europea de Porcelanas, which has been granted further aid, the Commission said.
The Commission said it believed there were aspects of the aid that could violate EU competition rules.
